front_blocks.md: Define a **saturated compound**.

back_blocks.md: A **saturated compound** is a molecule in which all carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds** (C-C). Alkanes are examples of saturated compounds.

cards.back_md: A **saturated compound** is a molecule in which all carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds** (C-C). Alkanes are examples of saturated compounds.

front_blocks.md: What is the general formula of the alkanes and the alkenes?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes have the general formula **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+2**</sub>. Alkenes have the general formula **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n**</sub>.

cards.front_md: What is the general formula of the alkanes and the alkenes?
cards.back_md: Alkanes have the general formula **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+2**</sub>. Alkenes have the general formula **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n**</sub>.

front_blocks.md: Define an **unsaturated compound**.

back_blocks.md: An **unsaturated compound** is a molecule in which one or more carbon-carbon bonds are **not** single bonds. Alkenes contain a carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) and are examples of unsaturated compounds.

cards.back_md: An **unsaturated compound** is a molecule in which one or more carbon-carbon bonds are **not** single bonds. Alkenes contain a carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) and are examples of unsaturated compounds.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Alkanes are **saturated** hydrocarbons. They contain only **single** carbon-carbon bonds (C-C). It is **alkenes** that are unsaturated because they contain a C=C double bond.

front_blocks.md: Define **homologous series**.

back_blocks.md: A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds that share the same functional group, have the same general formula, have similar chemical properties, and show a trend in physical properties.

cards.back_md: A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds that share the same functional group, have the same general formula, have similar chemical properties, and show a trend in physical properties.

front_blocks.md: What is the functional group of the alkenes, and what does the name ending reveal about the family?

back_blocks.md: The functional group of the **alkenes** is the carbon-carbon double bond (C=C). Alkene names end in **-ene**, which identifies the compound as belonging to this homologous series.

cards.front_md: What is the functional group of the alkenes, and what does the name ending reveal about the family?
cards.back_md: The functional group of the **alkenes** is the carbon-carbon double bond (C=C). Alkene names end in **-ene**, which identifies the compound as belonging to this homologous series.

front_blocks.md: Define **functional group**.

back_blocks.md: A **functional group** is a group of atoms bonded in a specific arrangement that is responsible for the characteristic reactions of an organic homologous series. For example, the C=C bond is the functional group of alkenes.

cards.back_md: A **functional group** is a group of atoms bonded in a specific arrangement that is responsible for the characteristic reactions of an organic homologous series. For example, the C=C bond is the functional group of alkenes.

front_blocks.md: Members of a homologous series have the same **..........**  and the same **..........**  formula, but show a trend in physical properties.

back_blocks.md: Members of a homologous series have the same **functional group** and the same **general** formula, but show a trend in physical properties.

cards.front_md: Members of a homologous series have the same **..........**  and the same **..........**  formula, but show a trend in physical properties.
cards.back_md: Members of a homologous series have the same **functional group** and the same **general** formula, but show a trend in physical properties.

front_blocks.md: Why do members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties?

back_blocks.md: Members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties because they all contain the **same functional group**. The functional group is responsible for the characteristic reactions of the series.

cards.front_md: Why do members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties?
cards.back_md: Members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties because they all contain the **same functional group**. The functional group is responsible for the characteristic reactions of the series.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All members of a homologous series have identical physical properties.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Members of a homologous series show a **trend** in physical properties. For example, boiling point, melting point, and viscosity all increase as molecule size increases.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

All members of a homologous series have identical physical properties.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Members of a homologous series show a **trend** in physical properties. For example, boiling point, melting point, and viscosity all increase as molecule size increases.

front_blocks.md: How does the boiling point change as molecules in a homologous series get larger, and why?

back_blocks.md: Boiling point **increases** as molecules get larger. Larger molecules have stronger **intermolecular forces**, so more energy is needed to separate them.

cards.front_md: How does the boiling point change as molecules in a homologous series get larger, and why?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes and alkenes belong to the same homologous series.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Alkanes** and **alkenes** are different homologous series. Alkanes have the functional group C-C (single bond) and end in -ane; alkenes have the functional group C=C (double bond) and end in -ene.
